claims.text: Density functional theory calculations can be used for phase-stability optimization in materials with variable composition and processing conditions.
Density functional theory calculations can be used for microstructure refinement.
Density functional theory calculations can be used for property optimization.
Variable composition and processing conditions can be supplied as inputs to ab initio or density functional theory calculations.
Density functional theory calculations can predict thermodynamic stability.
Density functional theory calculations can predict kinetic pathways.
Using density functional theory calculations will improve phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization relative to trial-and-error approaches.
Density functional theory-guided optimization will increase material performance by at least 15% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The accuracy of density functional theory calculations may be limited by material-system complexity.
The accuracy or applicability of density functional theory calculations may be limited by available computational resources.
Strength, toughness, and conductivity are proposed as material-performance measurements for comparing the two approaches.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 15% performance increase, but the hypothesis is falsified only below a 10% increase. An observed improvement from 10% to less than 15% would violate the predicted outcome without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
